title: Exploring Preference-Guided Diffusion Model for Cross-Domain Recommendation

problem.claim: Cross-domain recommendation must transfer source-domain user preference to construct an informative target-domain user representation for cold-start users.

gap.claim: Prior methods mainly map features without explicitly modeling preference integration, while existing diffusion-based methods do not directly account for preference from other domains; consequently, the feasibility of diffusion models for cross-domain recommendation remains underexplored.

contributions.claim: DMCDR uses a preference encoder and step-by-step injection of source-domain preference guidance into the diffusion reverse process to generate a personalized target-domain user representation.
The study explores the impact of six diffusion-model-based variants on cross-domain recommendation.

author_reported_evidence.claim: Experiments on three real-world cross-domain recommendation scenarios reportedly show that DMCDR outperforms state-of-the-art methods and six diffusion-model-based variants.

narrative_sequence.summary: Cross-domain recommendation aims to alleviate cold-start issues by transferring source-domain user preference into target-domain representations.
Existing approaches typically integrate preference into source-domain representations and map those representations to the target domain.
These approaches do not explicitly model preference integration, and existing diffusion methods do not directly handle cross-domain preference transfer.
DMCDR encodes source-domain interaction history as preference guidance and injects it throughout the diffusion reverse process to generate target-domain user representations.
The authors report comparisons across three real-world scenarios against state-of-the-art methods and six diffusion-based variants.

source_observation.claim: The proposed method explicitly injects a source-domain preference guidance signal during the diffusion reverse process.

interpretation.claim: Representing preference transfer as a guided generation process may preserve more detailed preference information than mapping already-formed representations.

application.claim: For cross-domain cold-start tasks, consider integrating source-domain interaction history directly into the representation-generation process.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish whether this approach generalizes beyond the reported recommendation scenarios or which variants and conditions determine its advantage.

unknowns: Dataset identities, sizes, splits, and evaluation metrics are not specified.
The six diffusion-model-based variants and state-of-the-art baselines are not described.
Ablation results, implementation details, and statistical uncertainty are not provided.
